Hi team — thanks for the quick responses. A few answers to procurement questions and proposed commercial options so your AP/legal can evaluate: 

1) Invoice cadence: We support monthly invoicing by default for committed contracts. For annual commitments we can also invoice quarterly or annually if needed. Monthly invoice + blanket PO for the term is a common pattern and should work with your AP system.

2) Payment methods: We support card for self-serve pilots under $10k, ACH/wire for invoices, and PO numbers for invoiced billing. If you prefer AWS Marketplace for Hosted consumption, we can enable Marketplace listing for the Hosted SKU — note that marketplace pricing and procurement flow adds marketplace fees and may change invoicing terms.

3) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: 
- Hosted (SaaS): fastest on-ramp, usage-based billing, ideal for pilots and early production. No dedicated capacity guarantees.
- Dedicated (Reserved): reserved GPU pools, commit pricing (monthly/annual), predictable throughput and data isolation — often preferred when customers need consistent unit economics and enterprise SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated data and full control; typically requires longer lead times and additional professional services.

4) Commercial paths we recommend for Acme based on our call: 
- Pilot: Hosted on-card (if under $10k) to validate integration and latency.
- Initial contract: 12-month Dedicated commit (monthly invoices under a blanket PO) to meet your purchasing rule (> $50k) while giving predictable unit economics.
- Marketplace: Can be enabled for Hosted if you want procurement to manage via AWS Marketplace, but note it may limit certain contract flexibilities (custom SLAs, commits).

I attached a procurement checklist and a draft SOW to speed review. If procurement would like, I can prepare two commercial options: (A) 12-month Dedicated commit with monthly invoices + blanket PO, and (B) On-demand Hosted with monthly billing via Marketplace (if you prefer Marketplace flow). Which option would procurement like to see formalized?

Hi Jessica / procurement team — quick technical clarifications to help you pick between Hosted / Dedicated / Private for procurement: 

- Latency & throughput: If your feature needs sub-200ms tail latency at scale we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity; Hosted can meet many use cases but tail latency is not SLA-backed unless on a Dedicated plan.
- Data residency & audits: Hosted keeps data in our managed environment (we can offer region controls), Dedicated provides stronger isolation (dedicated GPU pools). Private/VPC is available if you require the instance inside your VPC or on-prem.
- Billing & commit fit: Dedicated is priced for commits (monthly/annual) which maps well to PO-based purchasing. Hosted is usage-on-demand and maps easily to Marketplace subscriptions, but commitments are limited.

If you confirm expected monthly token volume range for the pilot and production, we can size a dedicated commit tier and provide per-token cost estimates for both commit vs on-demand paths. Happy to run a short sizing call — Marissa, can we schedule with procurement next week?

Thanks,
